other.label: CBO cost estimate: H.R. 3632, Power Plant Reliability Act of 2025

summary: The Power Plant Reliability Act of 2025 modifies how the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) handles power plant retirements and grid reliability. It allows transmission organizations and state commissions to ask FERC to keep power plants open if closing them would harm the reliability of the bulk power system. The bill requires power plant owners to give five years of advance notice before retiring a generating unit and exempts actions taken to comply with FERC reliability orders from environmental laws.

affected_groups.effect: Must provide five years of advance notice before retiring certain generating units, may be ordered by FERC to continue operating for up to five years, and are entitled to compensation for additional operating costs.
affected_groups.group: Public utilities and power plant owners/operators

affected_groups.effect: Granted the ability to file complaints with FERC regarding potential service inadequacies, request extensions on FERC operation orders, and receive advance retirement notices.
Tasked with reviewing complaints, issuing orders to keep power plants operating, determining compensation rates, granting extensions, and making retirement notices publicly available.

key_provisions: Allows transmission organizations and state commissions to file complaints with FERC if interstate electric service is inadequate or likely to become so within five years.
Empowers FERC to order a power plant to stay open for up to five years, with options for extensions.
Requires FERC orders to determine necessary compensation rates and cost allocations for keeping a unit operating.
Requires power plant owners and operators to provide five years of advance notice before retiring an electric generating unit with a capacity of 5 megawatts or more, except in emergencies.
Exempts any actions taken by a party to comply with a FERC service order from federal, state, and local environmental laws and regulations.
missing_information: Specific details on the exact formula or method FERC must use to calculate compensation rates and cost allocations.
Specific penalties or enforcement mechanisms for failing to provide the mandatory five-year retirement notice, other than the text noting exemptions from environmental liabilities.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Power Plant Reliability Act of 2025 modifies how the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) handles power plant retirements and grid reliability. It allows transmission organizations and state commissions to ask FERC to keep power plants open if closing them would harm the reliability of the bulk power system. The bill requires power plant owners to give five years of advance notice before retiring a generating unit and exempts actions taken to comply with FERC reliability orders from environmental laws.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters regulatory control over electricity generation and environmental compliance by granting federal authorities the power to override power plant retirements to protect grid reliability. Because compliance actions are exempted from environmental laws and power plants can be forced to stay open for up to five years, the legislation impacts energy market operations, utility planning, and environmental enforcement.

title: Power Plant Reliability Act of 2025
